questions.cardText:
[Ecology] What term describes the maximum sustainable size of a population that an environment can support without degradation?
A. Habitat limit
B. Ecological limit
C. Carrying capacity
Answer: C.
questions.en: What term describes the maximum population size of a species that an environment can sustain with its available food, water and habitat?
questions.de: Welcher Begriff bezeichnet die maximale Populationsgröße einer Art, die eine Umwelt mit ihrer verfügbaren Nahrung, ihrem Wasser und Lebensraum dauerhaft tragen kann?

timeline.labelEn: First recorded English use of the term 'carrying capacity', in a US Secretary of State report
timeline.labelDe: Erste belegte Verwendung des englischen Begriffs „carrying capacity“ in einem Bericht des US-Außenministers

questions.notes: Card answer confirmed. German term: Tragfähigkeit (ökologische Kapazität, Umweltkapazität; symbol K in the Verhulst model).

questions.cardText:
[Physiology and Anatomy] What is the primary function of the hypothalamus in the human brain?
A. Regulating vision and hearing
B. Maintaining homeostasis
C. Controlling balance and coordination
Answer: B. The hypothalamus maintains homeostasis and regulates essential functions such as temperature control, hunger, sleep, and emotional activity. Its functions can be summarized as the “four Fs”: fighting, fleeing, feeding, and mating.
questions.en: Which small part of the brain, linked to the pituitary gland, maintains homeostasis by controlling body temperature, hunger, thirst and sleep?
questions.de: Welcher kleine, mit der Hirnanhangdrüse verbundene Teil des Gehirns erhält die Homöostase aufrecht, indem er Körpertemperatur, Hunger, Durst und Schlaf steuert?

timeline.labelEn: Walter B. Cannon coins the term 'homeostasis', the internal balance the hypothalamus maintains
timeline.labelDe: Walter B. Cannon prägt den Begriff „Homöostase“ – das innere Gleichgewicht, das der Hypothalamus aufrechterhält

questions.notes: Reworked to name the organ from its function. Card answer confirmed (the hypothalamus controls body temperature, hunger, thirst, fatigue, sleep and circadian rhythms and links the nervous and endocrine systems via the pituitary). Timeline uses Cannon's 1926 coining of 'homeostasis' (Wikipedia, Homeostasis), as the hypothalamus itself has no single datable discovery.
